items.title: Chick Corea — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: One of the first bands I put together that I was real excited about was the band that finally made my first recording, Tones For Joan’s Bones, with Steve Swallow, Joe Farrell, Joe Chambers, and Woody Shaw.

ctx.x: You’re segueing me into something I’m very curious about, which is that you’re beginning to write, and you’re making recordings of original music at this time. I’m wondering if you can discuss this process.

Well, all the way through the early ‘60s, I was gigging and doing all these various things, but I loved to write. Just recently, I’ve come around to the realization that that was really my main—and still is—focus, was as a composer, and that piano never was the thing... Like, trying to be the great pianist was not ever my... I mean, I would love to now be a great pianist, so I’m starting to practice. But my focus was always composing, and I would use the piano to realize my compositions. So all through the early…
Was that band able to play gigs, or was it just a recording...
